bridge_policy.reserve_basis: Analyst 3% of $6.3B FY26 revenue, included in operating investment rather than excess cash.

bridge_policy.operating_leases: Rental cost remains in economic EBIT. Do not also subtract operating lease liability. Reconcile current lease liability if switching to financing treatment.
bridge_policy.tax: Cash tax-rate scenarios fund recurring operating taxes. Do not add full deferred-tax assets on top. Opening non-operating uncertain tax claims and transaction-tax settlement require explicit review.
bridge_policy.nqdc: Exclude trust asset credit because corresponding employee liability is embedded in other accrued liabilities.
bridge_policy.awards: Allocate assumed June unissued legacy RSU/PSU/LTP, options and ESPP rights once. Already-issued restricted shares are inside275.393 legal shares. Future new-grant economic value remains an operating expense. No deduction of970.8 unrecognized accounting expense.
bridge_policy.acquisitions: Hexagon closed before origin. Its cash and shares are already reflected; no second purchase-price deduction. July 2026 forecast includes integrated business. Future M&A has no growth contribution and no unfunded spend assumption.
bridge_policy.buybacks: No arbitrary future share shrinkage. Repurchases are capital allocation, not operating value creation.

conditional_assumptions.claim_budget_scope: All opening non-operating tax/transaction-tax, pension deficit, unpaid acquisition/retention, accrued financing interest, unmatched deferred-compensation and other non-operating derivative/contingent claims not already paid or funded elsewhere. No other listed claim is deducted outside this budget. Ordinary trade payables, recurring compensation, deferred revenue, operating leases and future integration/service cost remain in operating cash flow; they are not deducted as extra claims.
conditional_assumptions.overlap_policy: Gross UTB100.941 and9.941 accrued interest/penalties are not separately added on top of tax accrual reference amounts. NQDC trust is not credited; its matched liability is not separately deducted. Only any unmatched shortfall belongs within the budget. Hexagon consideration already paid is never charged again.
conditional_assumptions.budget_conditions: The500 default is an assumed aggregate settlement allowance, not a verified liability valuation. It assumes operating FCFF contains no additional settlement of the same opening non-operating claims and that ordinary liabilities are covered through operating costs/NWC. Unknown amounts and overlaps prevent proof that500 suffices.
conditional_assumptions.award_conditions: February19 unissued maximum award and option quantities are explicitly assumed unchanged at June30 for the base. Actual intervening grants, settlements and forfeitures are not reconstructed. Existing ESPP rights0.30M are an assumption anchored to0.284404M January purchases, not a June count. This is conditional alignment, not a source-dated June inventory.
conditional_assumptions.full_share_allocation: Treat all assumed legacy performance units as vesting at maximum. Options and ESPP rights are conservatively allocated as zero-price full shares with no proceeds credit; this is an upper participation convention for that assumed inventory, not option fair value and not proof of inventory completeness. Issued restricted shares are already in legal common and never added again.
irreducible_gaps: Exact June grant/vesting/forfeiture and issued-versus-unissued award rollforward, including current ESPP offering.
June current and long-term non-operating tax, pension, employee-retention and acquisition claims disaggregation; closing transaction-tax estimate is not an unpaid balance.

compensation.purpose: Separate already-granted award allocation from recurring economic cost of grants made after the June 30 origin. All amounts USD millions/shares millions unless stated.
compensation.proxy_limitations: Gross quantity times weighted grant-date fair value, before forfeitures. ESPP purchase quantities proxy grant quantities across overlapping offerings; performance accounting quantities are not maximum contractual settlement units. These are approximate annual grant-value proxies, neither exact total grants nor amortized GAAP expense.
compensation.future_grant_cost_policy: Post-origin new-grant value is an economic labor expense at 12%/10.2%/9% of revenue for downside/base/upside. The base approximates the three-year revenue-weighted proxy. No future-grant units are added again to the denominator. R&D remains expensed and includes its allocated grant cost; overlapping R&D and SBC percentages must not be summed.
compensation.stub_policy: FY26 guidance accounting SBC569 less H1 actual285.073 gives H2 accounting SBC283.927. Add that accounting amount back, then charge post-origin economic new-grant cost against H2 revenue. This is a replacement, never a free SBC add-back. Existing awards are allocated separately. H1 actual earnings/cash are not restated or valued twice.
compensation.annual_policy: Hold each v2 pre-SBC operating margin fixed. Replace its embedded SBC percentage with the new future-grant percentage, reducing base margins by1.2 percentage points. No offsetting cut to other costs. Recompute NOPAT and funded reinvestment under the unchanged incremental-return policy.

compensation.tax_policy: Scenario normalized cash-tax rates apply to economic operating profit. No separate legacy-vesting tax windfall or deferred-tax asset credit.

drivers: More custom silicon and design complexity increase verification/simulation requirements.
Agent products can monetize new workflow layers and increase underlying tool usage; independent incremental revenue remains unquantified.
Hardware capacity expands verification throughput; manufacturing and inventory make it less purely asset-light.
Advanced-node interfaces and foundry enablement support IP; customer milestones and licensing can be lumpy.
SDA expansion combines electrical and mechanical simulation, with acquisition integration and license-model transition risks.
risks: China export changes; H1 China growth contains weak 2025 comparison.
AI efficiency might reduce per-design effort; management assumes expanded design exploration more than offsets it.
Large foundry partnerships increase execution and R&D obligations; do not book announced partnership TAM as revenue.
Hexagon operating and revenue-recognition model transition can dilute earnings before growth.
Reported non-GAAP earnings remove SBC and integration costs that remain economic expenses in this model.

research.public_interview_synthesis: At the September 9 Goldman Sachs event, Devgan described AI agents as an additional subscription/consumption layer above physics-based tools. His thesis is that more design experiments and growing chip complexity sustain tool demand even when individual workflows accelerate. Hardware capacity and advanced-node interfaces were presented as additional drivers. These are management expectations; the interview does not supply a separately auditable AI revenue forecast. Source is a third-party transcript, with official event identity verified; audio was not independently transcribed.
research.call_QA_synthesis: Q2 discussion emphasized broad software/add-on demand, delivery timing in IP, hardware supply constraints, and investment in Intel opportunities and Hexagon integration. Management did not quantify an abrupt agentic-AI revenue step-up. The model therefore fades growth rather than treating product demonstrations or customer engagement counts as contracted sales.
